overview: LiquidSense Dev's Jesus walks on water with a motionY bounce cycle and no collision override and no onGround spoof. While the player's feet are in liquid and the sneak key is not held, the handler alternates between three ticks of a small 0.09 upward velocity and a single 0.5 burst that throws the feet above the surface, and a wasWater flag arms an ascent multiplier on the way up: any positive motionY while wasWater is set is scaled by 1.267 when it is at or below 0.1027 and then gets 0.05172 added. The result is a two-phase bob: slow hover ticks keep the player from sinking, the burst clears the surface, and the multiplier sustains the climb. Because the module only writes motionY, the wire fingerprint is the C03 position stream carrying the bounce's vertical deltas.

sections.p: The state machine is three fields: wasWater, ticks and the motionY writes. On any tick where the player is on the ground or on a ladder, wasWater resets to false. When isInLiquid() reports the feet inside liquid and the sneak key is up, ticks below 3 set motionY to 0.09 and increment ticks, and on the fourth tick motionY is set to 0.5, ticks resets to 0 and wasWater becomes true. The 0.09 value is just above the vanilla liquid sink rate, so the three hover ticks roughly hold the player's depth, and the 0.5 burst is a quarter-block per tick upward impulse, about 25 times the 0.02 liquid gravity, which lifts the feet out of the column in one or two ticks.

The wasWater flag does not just record the burst: while it is set and motionY is positive, the handler scales motionY by 1.267 whenever it is at or below 0.1027 and then adds a flat 0.05172. Applied to the 0.09 hover value that produces 0.09 times 1.267 plus 0.05172, about 0.166 per tick, so the climb from the burst is reinforced on every subsequent upward tick until the player reaches the surface and the horizontal walk takes over. The constant 0.1027 is the threshold that separates slow liquid motion from faster motion, and the flat 0.05172 addend guarantees the multiplier branch never stalls on a zero input.

The module sends no packets of its own and never touches the onGround flag. The server observes the bounce through the vanilla C03 stream: a position update every tick whose vertical delta alternates between the small hover steps and the 0.5 burst. To a liquid-physics model that reads as impossible vertical motion while the feet are in the column, which is exactly the gap the movement checks target. The sneak guard is the module's own bypass surface: holding sneak disables the whole handler, which is how a user walks into water legitimately without the bounce signature.

files.label: Jesus.java
files.explanation: The module is a single onUpdate handler with a three-field state machine. The ground and ladder reset, the isInLiquid and sneak gates, the ticks counter and the wasWater flag all live in one method. The ascent multiplier applies whenever motionY is positive and wasWater is set: the 1.267 factor is conditional on motionY being at or below 0.1027, and the 0.05172 addend always applies. The two motion writes (0.09 for the hover ticks, 0.5 for the burst) are the only places the module touches the player's physics. The description string is the terse ': /' the LiquidSense Dev snapshot uses for several modules.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (isInLiquid detector)
files.explanation: The static import isInLiquid is the module's only dependency. The detector first checks mc.thePlayer.isInWater(), the vanilla eye-level water check, and falls back to a bounding-box scan: it walks every column cell the entity bounding box covers at the box's minY and requires every non-air block there to be a BlockLiquid (lines 180-202). Any solid block in the row makes the scan return false, so the predicate reports liquid only when the feet row is uniformly water or lava. The module gates its entire bounce cycle on this predicate, so the surface-detection behavior is defined by this helper.

countering.label: Flight (Jesus)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Flight check, inside the ascending or descending branch, tests the destination with LocationHelper.isInLiquid and compares the client-claimed onGround flag against the server-computed ground state; when the client claims onGround while in liquid and the vertical speed is positive, the check names itself Flight (Jesus) and flags walking on water with the ccground_liquid reason (lines 266-272). The LiquidSense module never claims onGround, so that named branch does not fire; what does fire is the surrounding vertical logic, because a 0.5-block vertical step in one tick with no jump input is impossible motion in any branch of the check. The module's exposure is the raw vertical delta, not the ground claim.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (liquid envelope)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus SurvivalFly switches to the liquid physics model when the server-side position is in water: the horizontal allowance comes from estimateNextSpeed with WATER_HORIZONTAL_INERTIA and LIQUID_ACCELERATION, and the vertical side applies the 0.02 legacy liquid gravity for 1.8 clients. The module's 0.5 burst presents a vertical delta of half a block against a liquid envelope that allows about 0.02 per tick, an overshoot of roughly 25 times, so the violation (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 fires on the burst tick and the player is set back to the stored location. The hover ticks at 0.09 are closer to the model and can pass; the burst is what the envelope owns. The module keeps no server-side position offset, so every burst lands inside the column the check validates.

countering.label: SwimVertical (liquid vertical physics)
countering.explanation: Hawk SwimVertical models the in-liquid vertical physics: while the server-side player is swimming, the move delta Y must fall inside kinetic preservation (KINETIC_PRESERVATION_WATER 0.8) times the previous velocity plus or minus MOVE_LIQUID_FORCE (0.02) and the water flow force. The 0.5 burst is 25 times the liquid force bound, so each burst violates the prediction window and earns a punish with a rubberband. The 0.09 hover ticks sit near the legitimate window and the vanilla sink rate, so the check's pressure lands specifically on the burst tick, which means the module cannot hide its signature by slowing the hover phase; the burst is the mechanism that gets the feet out of the water.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (faked ground, boundary)
countering.explanation: Hawk GroundSpoof compares the client's claimed onGround flag against AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally, a server-side solid trace, and punishes the claim when the traced position is not solid unless a client-block placement or a boat explains it. The LiquidSense module never sets onGround true while on water, so this check does not fire on it: the module's design avoids the flag spoof entirely and relies on the bounce. That makes GroundSpoof the boundary of the countering set: the module is invisible to flag-based checks, and its exposure is entirely the vertical physics checks above. The honest read is that a bounce Jesus trades the onGround contradiction for a vertical-delta contradiction, and the physics checks are the ones that own it.
